note: Fresh-scenario generation architecture. This file does NOT create assessment items and does NOT weaken any exposure rule. It defines the variation dimensions that a generator (human or AI-assisted, see scripts/build_variants.py) must change to produce a genuinely different case, plus the validation metadata a future calibration step would need. A variant is only a candidate for the bank: it still has to be authored, source-checked, safety-reviewed, and calibrated before it can sit in assessments/bank.json. CRITICAL: changing a number alone is explicitly NOT sufficient variation - see minimum_meaningful_change below.

context.label: Setting and who is involved
context.description: Who the situation involves and where it happens, beyond the raw numbers.
examples: First job as a hospital cleaner rather than retail
Housing search in a different kind of tenancy
Money issue for someone caring for a relative

constraints.label: Hard limits or competing requirements
constraints.description: A rule, deadline, budget cap or competing demand that forces a real trade-off.
examples: Move date moved forward by two weeks
Only one evening available to view the property
Fixed appointment time that cannot move

trade-offs.label: Two good things that cannot both happen
trade-offs.description: A genuine dilemma where any answer has a cost - the point of the adaptation layer.
examples: Pay the deposit or keep the emergency fund
Attend the training or keep the shift
Fix the immediate problem or stop the recurring cause

missing-information.label: Something genuinely unknown
missing-information.description: A fact the learner must notice is absent and must handle by asking, verifying, or stating the assumption - rather than inventing.
examples: Cancellation terms not stated
Shift pattern only known for the first fortnight
Whether a repair is the landlord's responsibility

ambiguity.label: More than one reasonable reading
ambiguity.description: The case admits genuine interpretation, so the learner must say which reading they used and why.
examples: 'Available now' that could mean tonight or next month
A vague notice period that could be read two ways

irrelevant-information.label: Detail that looks relevant but is not
irrelevant-information.description: A distractor the learner must recognise and set aside, rather than being pulled into.
examples: An unrelated annual statement included in the post
A tempting but irrelevant discount

timing.label: When things happen
timing.description: Sequence, deadlines and lead times, as distinct from quantities.
examples: Deadline in 3 days vs 6 weeks
Payment falls just after payday vs just before
Problem occurs at the worst possible moment

error-trap.label: A plausible wrong turn
error-trap.description: A specific, tempting mistake a knowledgeable learner could still make, used to surface the competency's error tags.
examples: Comparing only the headline rent
Assuming a discount is permanent
Treating a monthly figure as the total cost
error-trap.status: declared for generation; not yet a bank axis

decision-type.label: The kind of decision being made
decision-type.description: Choose between options, verify a claim, escalate, prioritise, or decline.
examples: Compare and choose
Verify before acting
Decide whether to escalate now
Decide to decline
decision-type.status: declared for generation; not yet a bank axis

difficulty.label: Depth of reasoning required
difficulty.description: Single-step vs multi-step, and whether the answer survives one reversal.
examples: One reversal mid-task
Must hold a decision through a change and say whether it still holds
difficulty.status: declared for generation; not yet a bank axis

access-requirement.label: An access or practical constraint
access-requirement.description: Something that changes how the task must be done or evidenced, without lowering the standard.
examples: The only viewing is stairs-only and the learner uses a wheelchair
No reliable internet, so verification must happen by phone
Response must be spoken rather than written
access-requirement.status: declared for generation; not yet a bank axis
access-requirement.note: Access changes the route to evidence, never the standard of the evidence. Record via access_supports.

locality.label: Jurisdiction-specific rule or service
locality.description: A rule, service or protection that differs by nation. Never substituted across jurisdictions.
examples: Wales-specific tenancy or council services
UK-unspecified with no nation assumed
locality.status: controlled by eligibility/jurisdiction rules, not by free text
locality.note: Never generate a nation-specific variant without verified source coverage for that nation.

numbers.label: Quantities
numbers.description: The amounts and figures in the case.
examples: Different rent
A different balance
A different unexpected cost
numbers.status: NOT sufficient on its own to make a case fresh
numbers.note: Changing only numbers does not create meaningful variation. See minimum_meaningful_change.

wording.label: Surface phrasing
wording.description: How the same underlying decision is worded.
examples: A letter rather than a text
A different persona
wording.status: weak on its own; pairs with a meaningful axis

minimum_meaningful_change.rule: A variant must change at least one of: context, constraints, trade-offs, missing-information, ambiguity, irrelevant-information, timing, error-trap, decision-type, difficulty. Changing quantities alone (the numbers) is NOT sufficient and must be rejected; a numbers- or wording-only change does not create a fresh case.
minimum_meaningful_change.why: The retention promise is four intervals of fresh independent material. If variants differ only by arithmetic, a learner can pass a later check without having re-applied the decision, which would overstate real transfer.

variant_metadata_contract.note: Every generated variant carries this metadata so it can be validated, calibrated and traced later. It is intentionally reviewable by a human.

fields.name: base_item_id
fields.note: The canonical item this was derived from.

fields.name: variant_axes
fields.note: Which dimensions changed; must include at least one from the meaningful set.

fields.name: variant_digest
fields.note: Stable hash of the variant's context/constraint/trap payload, used to detect accidental duplicate cases.

fields.name: jurisdictions
fields.note: Only jurisdictions with verified source coverage.

fields.name: expected_error_tags
fields.note: Which existing competency error tags this variant is designed to surface.

fields.name: calibration_status
fields.note: Only 'calibrated' variants may enter the bank.

generation_prompts.note: These are the standing instructions used when AI assists generation. The AI may propose candidate situations and explanations; it may never grade, derive outcomes, or alter the deterministic engine. Every generated candidate is authored, source-checked and calibrated by a human before use. See docs/product.md#ai-boundaries.
system_rules: Do not produce a final answer, mark a criterion, or suggest an outcome. Generate the SITUATION only.
Do not change only the numbers. Change at least one contextual, constraint, missing-information, trade-off, timing or decision-type dimension.
Keep every number fictional and non-identifying.
Never produce guidance specific to a nation unless a verified source for that nation is supplied.
Attach the expected existing error tags and the metadata contract fields.
Flag any safety, consent or regulated topic so a human reviews it before it is considered.
